verses.1: Having stayed that night in Keshini, Lakshmana, the delight of the Raghus, rose again in the morning and then departed.
verses.2: Then, at midday, the great warrior Lakshmana entered Ayodhya, which was full of jewels and teeming with happy and well-nourished people.
verses.3: The highly intelligent Lakshmana was overcome with extreme distress, wondering what he would say to Rama upon reaching his feet.
verses.4: As he was thus contemplating, Rama's most magnificent palace, shining like the moon, appeared before him.
verses.5: At the king's palace gate, he alighted from his excellent chariot and, with a downcast face and sorrowful mind, entered unhindered.
verses.6: He saw Rama, his elder brother, seated on an excellent seat in front of him, looking distressed, and his own eyes filled with tears.
verses.7: Lakshmana, with a sorrowful mind, grasped Rama's feet and, with folded hands and a very composed yet humble voice, began to speak.
verses.8: Having followed your command, I left Janaka's daughter on the pure bank of the Ganga, in Valmiki's hermitage as instructed.
verses.9: O hero, I have returned to serve at your feet, having left her, who is of auspicious conduct and glorious, there at the edge of the hermitage.
verses.10: O tiger among men, do not grieve, for such is the course of time, and intelligent, high-minded individuals like you certainly do not lament.
verses.11: All accumulations end in decay, all elevations end in a fall, all unions end in separation, and life itself ends in death.
verses.12: Therefore, one should not have excessive attachment to sons, wives, friends, or wealth, for separation from them is indeed inevitable.
verses.13: O Kakutstha, you are surely capable of controlling your own self and indeed all worlds by your mind, so how much more easily can you control your own sorrow?
verses.14: Best among men like you do not become bewildered in such situations, and indeed, O Raghava, that very blame will come upon you again.
verses.15: O King, that very blame for which Maithili was abandoned out of fear of scandal will undoubtedly arise again among the people in the city.
verses.16: O best of men, you, being well-composed with fortitude, should abandon this weak thought and indeed do not give in to grief.
verses.17: Thus addressed by the great-souled Lakshmana, that Kakutstha, who was affectionate towards his friends, spoke to Saumitri with great affection.
verses.18: O best among men, Lakshmana, this is indeed as you say, and I am greatly satisfied, O hero, with your counsel regarding my duty.
verses.19: O gentle Lakshmana, relief has come, and my sorrow has been dispelled; I have been comforted by your very pleasing words. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे द्विपञ्चाशः सर्गः ।। 52 ।। Thus ends the fifty-second sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
